definitions.explanation: A shop that sells ready-made dishes and side dishes for takeout. These stores typically offer a variety of cooked foods such as fried items, salads, simmered dishes, and rice balls.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{総菜屋|そうざいや}で{買|か}い{物|もの}をした。
examples.english: I shopped at the deli in front of the station.

examples.japanese: あの{総菜屋|そうざいや}のコロッケはとても{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: The croquettes at that deli are very popular.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{日|ひ}は{総菜屋|そうざいや}で{夕飯|ゆうはん}のおかずを{買|か}って{帰|かえ}ることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: On busy days, I often buy side dishes for dinner at the deli on my way home.

notes:
Compound of {総菜|そうざい} (side dishes, prepared food) + {屋|や} (shop/store). Refers to shops specializing in ready-made dishes for takeout.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {総菜屋|そうざいや}で{買|か}う: to buy at a deli
- {町|まち}の{総菜屋|そうざいや}: neighborhood deli
- {手作|てづく}り{総菜屋|そうざいや}: handmade-food shop

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional {総菜屋|そうざいや} have long been a staple of Japanese neighborhoods, offering affordable home-style cooking. While supermarket deli sections ({惣菜|そうざい}コーナー) and convenience stores have taken over much of this role, independent {総菜屋|そうざいや} remain popular for their quality and personal touch.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {惣菜|そうざい}: the prepared food itself ({惣|そう} and {総|そう} are variant kanji)
- {弁当屋|べんとうや}: boxed-lunch shop
